verses.sanskrit:
धृतराष्ट्र उवाच।
              सर्व एते महोत्साहा ये त्वया परिकीर्तिताः। एकतस्त्वेव ते सर्वे समेता भीम एकतः ॥१॥
verses.english: Dhritarashtra said All these who have been enumerated by you are of great energy and courage; but Bhima alone is equal to all of them combined.

verses.sanskrit: भीमसेनाद्धि मे भूयो भयं सञ्जायते महत्। क्रुद्धादमर्षणात्तात व्याघ्रादिव महारुरोः ॥२॥
verses.english: From Bhimasena wrathful I have very great fear like that of a large deer from an enraged tiger.

verses.sanskrit: जागर्मि रात्रयः सर्वा दीर्घमुष्णं च निःश्वसन्। भीतो वृकोदरात्तात सिंहात् पशुरिवापरः ॥३॥
verses.english: I am awake during entire nights breathing large and hot sighs, being afraid of Vrikodara, O dear, as any other animal fears a lion.

verses.sanskrit: न हि तस्य महाबाहोः शक्रप्रतिमतेजसः। सैन्येऽस्मिन् प्रतिपश्यामि य एनं विषहेद्युधि ॥४॥
verses.english: In this entire army do I not see one who can withstand in battle this one of long arms and having strength like that of Shakra.

verses.sanskrit: अमर्षणश्च कौन्तेयो दृढवैरश्च पाण्डवः। अनर्महासी सोन्मादस्तिर्यक्प्रेक्षी महास्वनः ॥५॥
verses.english: That son of Kunti and Pandu when wrathful is an implacable enemy; and he smiles not even in jest and is mad with rage, looks at things askance and is of loud voice,

verses.sanskrit: महावेगो महोत्साहो महाबाहुर्महाबलः। मन्दानां मम पुत्राणां युद्धेनान्तं करिष्यति ॥६॥
verses.english: Possessed of great force and of great energy, possessed of long arms and of great strength will put an end to the existence of any wicked sons in battle.
verses.bhavadeepa: अनर्महासी नर्म वृथोपहासः तदन्यो हासः सत्यमेव कृत्वा शत्रूनुपहसतीत्यर्थः ॥५॥

verses.sanskrit: उरुग्राहगृहीतानां गदां बिभ्रद्वृकोदरः। कुरूणामृषभो युद्धे दण्डपाणिरिवान्तकः ॥७॥
verses.english: Vrikodara, that bull in the race of Kuru, wielding the mace slay them struck by a heavy calamity in battle like the god of death with his staff in his hand.

verses.sanskrit: अष्टास्रिमायसीं घोरां गदां काञ्चनभूषणाम्। मनसाऽहं प्रपश्यामि ब्रह्मदण्डमिवोद्यतम् ॥८॥
verses.english: That terrible steel mace with eight sides and ornamented with gold I now see in my mind like the staff of Brahma uplifted.

verses.sanskrit: यथा मृगाणां यूथेषु सिंहो जातबलश्चरेत्। मामकेषु तथा भीमो बलेषु विचरिष्यति ॥९॥
verses.english: As a fully grown up lion roams among a hear of deer, so Bhima roam among my army.

verses.sanskrit: सर्वेषां मम पुत्राणां स एकः क्रूरविक्रमः। बह्वाशी विप्रतीपश्च बाल्येऽपि रभसः सदा ॥१०॥
verses.english: Towards all my sons he alone (of all his brothers) showed his cruel strength. A voracious eater and endued with great strength, even in his childhood was he inimical (to my sons).

verses.sanskrit: उद्वेपते मे हृदयं ये मे दुर्योधनादयः। बाल्येऽपि तेन युध्यन्तो वारणेनेव मर्दिताः ॥११॥
verses.english: My heart quakes that Duryodhana and other sons of mine even when fighting with him in their childhood were smashed as by elephants.

verses.sanskrit: तस्य वीर्येण सङ्क्लिष्टा नित्यमेव सुता मम। स एव हेतुर्भेदस्य भीमो भीमपराक्रमः ॥१२॥
verses.english: O pressed by his strength my sons have ever been; and that Bhima of terrible prowess is the cause of this rupture.

verses.sanskrit: ग्रसमानमनीकानिं नरवारणवाजिनाम्। पश्यामीवाग्रतो भीमं क्रोधमूर्छितमाहवे ॥१३॥
verses.english: Devouring my army composed of men, elephants and horses, do I see Bhima in the front senseless with wrath,

verses.sanskrit: अस्त्रे द्रोणार्जुनसमं वायुवेगसमं जवे। महेश्वरसमं क्रोधे को हन्याद्भीममाहवे ॥१४॥
verses.english: In arms equal of Drona and Arjuna and in speed having the force of wind, in wrath equal to Maheshvara himself, who will kill Bhima in battle.

verses.sanskrit: सञ्जयाचक्ष्व मे शूरं भीमसेनममर्षणम्। अतिलाभं तु मन्येऽहं यत्तेन रिपुघातिना ॥१५॥
verses.english: O Sanjaya, that hero, the wrathful Bhimasena; tell me that; it is a great gain I consider, that by that slayer of enemies.

verses.sanskrit: तदैव न हताः सर्वे पुत्रा मम मनस्विना। येन भीमबला यक्षा राक्षसाश्च पुरा हताः ॥१६॥
verses.english: My sons were not all killed by that one of independent mind by whom Yakshas of terrible strength and the Rakshasas were killed in days of old.

verses.sanskrit: कथं तस्य रणे वेगं मानुषः प्रसहिष्यति। न स जातु वशे तस्थौ मम बाल्येऽपि सञ्जय ॥१७॥
verses.english: How can a man withstand the force of him in battle. He was not under my control even in his childhood, O Sanjaya.

verses.sanskrit: किं पुनर्मम दुष्पुत्रैः क्लिष्टः सम्प्रति पाण्डवः। निष्ठुरो रोषणोऽत्यर्थं भज्येतापि न संनमेत्। तिर्यक्प्रेक्षी संहतभ्रूः कथं शाम्येद्वृकोदरः ॥१८॥
verses.english: How can that son of Pandu do so now having been wronged by my wicked sons. Cruel and wrathful, he could not bend even when broken. Looking at things ask once, with his eyebrows contracted how can Vrikodara be peaceful.

verses.sanskrit: शूरस्तथाऽप्रतिबलो गौरस्ताल इवोन्नतः। प्रमाणतो भीमसेनः प्रादेशेनाधिकोऽर्जुनात् ॥१९॥
verses.english: A hero of exceedingly white complexion and tall like the palm tree, Bhimasena measures a Prasesha (the span of a thumb) more than Arjuna.
verses.bhavadeepa: संहते क्रोधेन ग्रथिते भ्रुवौ यस्य संहतभ्रूः ॥१८॥

verses.sanskrit: जवेन वाजिनोऽत्येति बलेनात्येति कुञ्जरान्। अव्यक्तजल्पी मध्वक्षो मध्यमः पाण्डवो बली ॥२०॥
verses.english: Surpassing in speed the horses, in strength the elephants, the second son of Pandu who is of great strength has sweet eyes.

verses.sanskrit: इति बाल्ये श्रुतः पूर्वं मया व्यासमुखात् पुरा। रूपतो र्वार्यतश्चैव याथातथ्येन पाण्डवः ॥२१॥
verses.english: The Pandava in form and power just as I heard from the lips of Vyasa in days gone by.

verses.sanskrit: आयसेन स दण्डेन रथान्नागान्नरान् हयान्। हनिष्यति रणे क्रुद्धो रौद्रः क्रूरपराक्रमः ॥२२॥
verses.english: Easily by means of his mace, the chariots, the elephants, men and horses he will kill in battle, that terrible being when wrathful, that man of cruel purposes.
verses.bhavadeepa: इतीति । पुरा पुराणं निकटेऽतिदृढमिति वाऽर्थः । ‘पुरा पुराणेऽतिदृढे’ इति मेदिनी । ‘पुरा भाविपुराणयोः । प्रबन्धे निकटेऽतीते’ इति विश्वलोचनः ॥२१॥

verses.sanskrit: अमर्षी नित्यसंरब्धो भीमः प्रहरतां वरः। मया तात प्रतीपानि कुर्वन् पूर्वं विमानितः ॥२३॥
verses.english: That wrathful Bhima, who is ever furiousthat chief among the smiters has by acting against my wishes, O dear, before been insulted by me.

verses.sanskrit: निष्कर्णामायसीं स्थूलां सुपार्श्वां काञ्चनीं गदाम्। शतघ्नीं शतनिर्ह्रादां कथं शक्ष्यन्ति मे सुताः ॥२४॥
verses.english: That mace which has no curves, which is made of steel, which is of bulk, of beautiful sides, adorned with gold, which is capable of killing a hundred and when flung producing a terrible sound-how will my sons bears?

verses.sanskrit: अपारमप्लवागाधं समुद्रं शरवेधनम्। भीमसेनमयं दुर्गं तात मन्दास्तितीर्षवः ॥२५॥
verses.english: That inaccessible ocean, which has no shore, which is unfathomable and which has currents in the shape of Bhima, those wicked ones are desirous of crossing over.

verses.sanskrit: क्रोशतो मे न शृण्वन्ति बालाः पण्डितमानिनः। विषमं न हि मन्यन्ते प्रपातं मधुदर्शिनः ॥२६॥
verses.english: Those children thinking themselves to be wise do not listen to my words, even if I cry out. Seeing the honey (formerly collected on mountain tops) they do not care for the heavy fall.

verses.sanskrit: संयुगं ये गमिष्यन्ति नररूपेण मृत्युना। नियतं चोदिता धात्रा सिंहेनेव महामृगाः ॥२७॥
verses.english: Those who encounter in battle that death in human shape have their dooms settled by the father of the universe, like those of large deer encountering lions,

verses.sanskrit: शैक्यां तात चतुष्किष्कुं षडस्रिममितौजसम्। प्रहितां दुःखसंस्पर्शां कथं शक्ष्यन्ति मे सुताः ॥२८॥
verses.english: How shall my sons bear, Odear, the mace when flung at them the mace which is four cubits long, having six sides of illimitable powers of destruction and terrible to touch.

verses.sanskrit: गदां भ्रामयतस्तस्य भिन्दतो हस्तिमस्तकान्। सृक्किणी लेलिहानस्य बाष्पमुत्सृजतो मुहुः ॥२९॥
verses.english: Whirling the mace and piercing the heads of elephants, licking the corners of his lips and giving out (terrific) breaths every moment, making terrific noises in return of those of falling elephants and rushing with loud roars against elephants coming against him, having penetrated into the place where the chariots stand, when he kills the heroes after taking aim against them, will one of my soldiers escape from him who is blazing like fire?
verses.bhavadeepa: शैक्यां शिक्यस्थाम् । अधःपतनेन भूमिविदारणशङ्कया शिक्ये स्थापिताम् ॥२८॥

verses.sanskrit: उद्दिश्य नागान् पततः कुर्वतो भैरवान्रवान्। प्रतीपं पततो मत्तान् कुञ्जरान् प्रतिगर्जतः ॥३०॥
विगाह्य रथमार्गेषु वरानुद्दिश्य निघ्नतः। अग्नेः प्रज्वलितस्येव अपि मुच्येत मे प्रजा ॥३१॥
वीथीं कुर्वन्महाबाहुर्द्रावयन्मम वाहिनीम्। नृत्यन्निव गदापाणिर्युगान्तं दर्शयिष्यति ॥३२॥
verses.english: Grinding the four elements of my army and cutting his passage out through it, as if dancing with the mace in his hand, he will show (to people) the scene which takes place at the end of a Yuga (universal destruction).

verses.sanskrit: प्रभिन्न इव मातङ्गः प्रभञ्जन् पुष्पितान् द्रुमान्। प्रवेक्ष्यति रणे सेनां पुत्राणां मे वृकोदरः ॥३३॥
verses.english: Like an elephant mad with rage, breaking trees with flowers, Vrikodara will crush the army of my sons of battle.

verses.sanskrit: कुर्वन् रथान् विपुरुषान् विसारथिहयध्वजान्। आरुजन् पुरुषव्याघ्रो रथिनः सादिनस्तथा ॥३४॥
verses.english: Rendering the chariots devoid of men, drivers, horse and banners and giving trouble to the warriors fighting from cars and elephants, the tiger among men, like the force of the currents of the Ganga uprooting various sorts of trees, will vanquish in battle the army of my sons, O Sanjaya.

verses.sanskrit: गङ्गावेग इवानूपांस्तीरजान् विविधान् द्रुमान्। प्रभङ्क्ष्यति रणे सेनां पुत्राणां मम सञ्जय ॥३५॥
दिशो नूनं गमिष्यन्ति भीमसेनभयार्दिताः। मम पुत्राश्च भृत्याश्च राजानश्चैव सञ्जय ॥३६॥
verses.english: My with their servants and subordinate chiefs, O Sanjaya, troubled with the fear of Bhimasena will certainly fly in different directions.

verses.sanskrit: येन राजा महावीर्यः प्रविश्यान्तःपुरं पुरा। वासुदेवसहायेन जरासन्धो निपातितः ॥३७॥
verses.english: (That Bhimasena) by whom, aided by the son of Vasudeva, the king Jarasandha of great prowess was killed after his inner apartments being entered in the days of old.

verses.sanskrit: कृत्स्नेयं पृथिवी देवी जरासन्धेन धीमता। मागधेन्द्रेण बलिना वशे कृत्वा प्रतापिता ॥३८॥
verses.english: The goddess Earth was brought under control by the wise Jarasandha and that mighty Lord of Magadha, who subjugated her and oppressed her people.

verses.sanskrit: भीष्मप्रतापात् कुरवो नयेनान्धकवृष्णयः। यन्न तस्य वशे जग्मुः केवलं दैवमेव तत् ॥३९॥
verses.english: That the Kurus through the prowess of Bhima and the Andhakas and the Vrishnis and sons through their diplomacy, were not brought under subjection by them, which was only due to the gods.

verses.sanskrit: स गत्वा पाण्डुपुत्रेण तरसा बाहुशालिना। अनायुधेन वीरेण निहतः किं ततोऽधिकम् ॥४०॥
verses.english: The son of Pandu, the heroic of long arms, having approached him without any arms, killed him. What can be more (wonderful) than this?

verses.sanskrit: दीर्घकालसमासक्तं विषमाशीविषो यथा। स मोक्ष्यति रणे तेजः पुत्रेषु मम सञ्जय ॥४१॥
verses.english: Like venomous snake having accumulated its poison for a long time, he (Bhima) will fling his strength on my sons in the field of battle, O Sanjaya.

verses.sanskrit: महेन्द्र इव वज्रेण दानवान् देवसत्तमः। भीमसेनो गदापाणिः सूदयिष्यति मे सुतान् ॥४२॥
verses.english: Like that chief among the gods, great Indra with his thunderbolt (killing) the Danavas, Bhimasena with mace in his hand will kill my a sons.

verses.sanskrit: अविषह्यमनावार्यं तीव्रवेगपराक्रमम्। पश्यामीवातिताम्राक्षमापतन्तं वृकोदरम् ॥४३॥
verses.english: I see (in my mind) Vrikodara having eyes of the colour of copper, incapable of being opposed or prevented and having fearful force of strength falling on (my sons).

verses.sanskrit: अगदस्याप्यधनुषो विरथस्य विवर्मणः। बाहुभ्यां युद्ध्यमानस्य कस्तिष्ठेदग्रतः पुमान् ॥४४॥
verses.english: Who can stay in front of that man fighting with his two arms without mace or bow and without being on his car.

verses.sanskrit: भीष्मो द्रोणश्च विप्रोऽयं कृपः शारद्वतस्तथा। जानन्त्येते यथैवाहं वीर्यज्ञस्तस्य धीमतः ॥४५॥
verses.english: Bhishma, this regenerate Drona, Kripa and also the son of Shardavata-all these know as much as I do the prowess of that wise one.

verses.sanskrit: आर्यव्रतं तु जानन्तः सङ्गरान्तं विधित्सवः। सेनामुखेषु स्थास्यन्ति मामकानां नरर्षभाः ॥४६॥
verses.english: Conversant with the habits of life of the virtuous and desirous of death in battle, those bulls among men in our party will stand in front of the army.

verses.sanskrit: बलीयः सर्वतो दिष्टं पुरुषस्य विशेषतः। पश्यन्नपि जयं तेषां न नियच्छामि यत्सुतान् ॥४७॥
verses.english: Destiny is always powerful specially in a man through I see them (the Pandavas) victorious, yet I do not dissuade my sons.
verses.bhavadeepa: सङ्‌गरे अन्तं स्वस्य नाशम् । स्थास्यन्ति भीष्मादयः ॥४६॥

verses.sanskrit: ते पुराणं महेष्वासा मार्गमैन्द्रं समास्थिताः। त्यक्ष्यन्ति तुमुले प्राणान् रक्षन्तः पार्थिवं यशः ॥४८॥
verses.english: They (the warriors of our party), desirous of going along the eternal, noble and heavenly path, will part with their lives in fierce battle thus keeping your earthly fame unsullied.

verses.sanskrit: यथैषां मामकास्तात तथैषां पाण्डवा अपि। पौत्रा भीष्मस्य शिष्याश्च द्रोणस्य च कृपस्य च ॥४९॥
verses.english: As these are, O dear, to my sons, so are they to the Pandavas (in ties of blood and affection). They (the Pandavas) are grandsons of Bhishma and disciples of Drona and Kripa.

verses.sanskrit: ये त्वस्मदाश्रयं किञ्चिद्दत्तमिष्टं च सञ्जय। तस्यापचितिमार्यत्वात् कर्तारः स्थविरास्त्रयः ॥५०॥
verses.english: The protection that we have afforded to the three-aged ones, the little we have given them and the little good we have done to them, they will compensate us for that in return owing to their noble nature.

verses.sanskrit: आददानस्य शस्त्रं हि क्षत्रधर्मं परीप्सतः। निधनं क्षत्रियस्याजौ वरमेवाहुरुत्तमम् ॥५१॥
verses.english: That death of a Kshatriya is said to be a peaceful and commendable one, which is met with in battle when one takes up arms desirous of observing Kshatriya practices.

verses.sanskrit: स वै शोचामि सर्वान् वै ये युयुत्सन्ति पाण्डवैः। विक्रुष्टं विदुरेणादौ तदेतद्भयमागतम् ॥५२॥
verses.english: I grieve however for all those who will fight with the son of Pandu; the calamity prophesied by Vidura is now come.

verses.sanskrit: न तु मन्ये विघाताय ज्ञानं दुःखस्य सञ्जय। भवत्यतिबलं ह्येतज्ज्ञानस्याप्युपघातकम् ॥५३॥
verses.english: I consider, O Sanjaya, that knowledge cannot destroy woe; in fact, it is excessive distress that kills knowledge.

verses.sanskrit: ऋषयो ह्यपि निर्मुक्ताः पश्यन्तो लोकसङ्ग्रहान्। सुखैर्भवन्ति सुखिनस्तथा दुःखेन दुःखिताः ॥५४॥
verses.english: Even the Rishis who are emancipated and who merely look on this crowd of men become happy at prosperity and aggrieved at adversity.
verses.bhavadeepa: एतत् भावि दुःखम् अतिबलं ज्ञानेन अनिवार्यम् ॥५३॥

verses.sanskrit: किं पुनर्मोहमासक्तस्तत्र तत्र सहस्रधा। पुत्रेषु राज्यदारेषु पौत्रेष्वपि च बन्धुषु ॥५५॥
verses.english: Why then should I not be affected by grief. When I ain attached to my sons, my kingdom, my wife, my grandsons, my friends and a thousand other objects.

verses.sanskrit: संशये तु महत्यस्मिन् किं नु मे क्षममुत्तरम्। विनाशं ह्येव पश्यामि कुरूणामनुचिन्तयन् ॥५६॥
verses.english: I have grave doubts that I shall have any prosperity in the future; thinking thus I see (in my mind) the destruction of the Kurus.

verses.sanskrit: द्यूतप्रमुखमाभाति कुरूणां व्यसनं महत्। मन्देनैश्वर्यकामेन लोभात् पापमिदं कृतम् ॥५७॥
verses.english: The great calamity of the Kurus beginning with the game at dice now stands out in bold relief; this wicked act has been done by that fool desiring for prosperity out of avarice.

verses.sanskrit: मन्ये पर्यायधर्मोऽयं कालस्यात्यन्तगामिनः। चक्रे प्रधिरिवासक्तो नास्य शक्यं पलायितुम् ॥५८॥
verses.english: I consider this to be the work of Eternal Time. I am not able to fly from it like the iron ring attached to the wheel.

verses.sanskrit: किन्नु कुर्यां कथं कुर्यां क्व नु गच्छामि सञ्जय। एते नश्यन्ति कुरवो मन्दाः कालवशं गताः ॥५९॥
verses.english: What shall I do? how shall I do it and where shall I go, O Sanjaya? These foolish Kurus will be destroyed being subject to the effects of time.
verses.bhavadeepa: पर्यायधर्मः विपरीतधर्मः । प्रधिर्नेमिः । अस्य कालवशस्य । तृतीयार्थे षष्ठी ॥५८॥

verses.sanskrit: अवशोऽहं तदा तात पुत्राणां निहते शते। श्रोष्यामि निनदं स्त्रीणां कथं मां मरणं स्पृशेत् ॥६०॥
verses.english: I shall be helpless, O dear, on my hundred sons being killed and shall hear the loud lamentation of women. How shall death touch me?

verses.sanskrit: यथा निदाघे ज्वलनः समिद्धो दहेत् कक्षं वायुना चोद्यमानः। गदाहस्तः पाण्डवो वै तथैव हन्ता मदीयान् सहितोऽर्जुनेन ॥६१॥
verses.english: As in the hot season a fire ignited and urged by wind burns up dry grass, so will the son of Pandu, having mace in hand along with Arjuna, be the slayer of my party.
